name: Rwanda
headline: Rwanda: +9.4% growth in 2025, 7.0% inflation, debt 65% of GDP
sections: Rwanda is a $16.4 billion economy (2025), the world's 144th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +9.4% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $4,164 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.3% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 7.0% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 13.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 11.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 16.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 65% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −4.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −9.8% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 57% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 5.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 60% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 68.0 years (2024). Population: 14.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
